[[Charleston Classic]] champions |bowl = [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = Second Round }} {{2016–17 Big East men's basketball standings}} The '''2016–17 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented [[Villanova University]] in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Led by head coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]] in his 16th year, the Wildcats participated in the [[Big East Conference]] and played their home games at [[Finneran Pavilion|The Pavilion]], with some select home games at the [[Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)|Wells Fargo Center]] in [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]. They finished the season 32–4, 15–3 in [[2016–17 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]] to win the regular season championship. In the [[2017 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], they defeated [[2016–17 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]], [[2016–17 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]], and [[2016–17 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] to win the tournament championship.{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/big-east-tournament-2017-scores-bracket-live-blog-villanova-to-face-creighton-in-title-game/|title=Big East tournament 2017 scores, bracket: Villanova makes statement with dominant title win|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en}} As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. The Wildcats were given the Tournament's overall No. 1 seed as a No. 1 seed in the East region. In the First Round they defeated [[2016–17 Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball team|Mount St. Mary's]] before being upset by No. 8-seeded [[2016–17 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the Second Round.{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/03/18/wisconsin-villanova-badgers-wildcats-upset-ncaa-tournament|title=Down goes Villanova: No. 8 seed Wisconsin stuns the reigning national champs|last=Greene|first=Dan|work=SI.com|access-date=2017-07-14}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/march-finally-gives-us-some-madness-as-wisconsin-ousts-villanova-3-takeaways/|title=March finally gives us some madness as Wisconsin ousts Villanova: 3 takeaways|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en}} The loss marked the second time in the previous three tournaments that Villanova was upset by an eighth-seeded team. The season marked the final season for The Pavilion before its temporary closure for a $60 million renovation project.{{Cite news|url=http://www.phillymag.com/news/2017/02/16/villanova-pavilion-renovation-basketball-gym/|title=Villanova Plans $60 Million Makeover of Pavilion|date=2017-02-16|work=Philadelphia Magazine|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en-US}} It reopened for the 2018–19 season with the new name of Finneran Pavilion after a Villanova alum who donated $22.6 million to Villanova.{{cite press release|url=http://www.villanova.com/genrel/021417aac.html |title=Board of Trustees Approves Pavilion Renovation |publisher=[[Villanova Wildcats]] |date=February 14, 2017 |accessdate=March 30, 2017}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.vuhoops.com/2017/2/14/14612240/villanova-basketball-finneran-pavilion-renovation-announced-60-million|title=Villanova Basketball Pavilion Renovation Approved|work=VU Hoops|access-date=2017-07-14}} All home games for the 2017–18 season were played at the [[Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)|Wells Fargo Center]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.villanova.com/genrel/021417aac.html|title=Board of Trustees Approves Pavilion Renovation|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en}} ==Previous season== The [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] with a record of 35–5, 16–2 in [[2015–16 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]] to win the Big East regular season championship. In the [[2016 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] they defeated [[2015–16 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] and [[2015–16 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]], but lost to [[2015–16 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]] in the championship game.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/112323/seton-hall-wins-big-east-championship-puts-villanovas-no-1-seed-in-peril|title=Seton Hall wins Big East championship, puts Villanova's No. 1 seed in peril|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-07-14}} The Wildcats received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], being awarded the No. 2 seed in the South Region. Villanova defeated [[2015–16 UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball team|UNC Asheville]] and [[2015–16 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. In the Sweet Sixteen, they defeated [[2015–16 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]] and upset overall No. 1 seed [[2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] in the Elite Eight to advance to the fifth Final Four in school history.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400873025|title=Villanova vs. Kansas - Game Recap - March 26, 2016 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-07-14}} In the Final Four, the Wildcats defeated [[2015–16 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]] to advance to the school's third [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|National Championship game]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/march-madness/index.ssf/2016/04/ncaa_tournament_2016_scores_fi.html|title=Final Four 2016 scores: Villanova crushes Oklahoma; North Carolina rolls Syracuse|work=OregonLive.com|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en-US}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/04/03/sports/ncaabasketball/villanova-oklahoma-final-four-ncaa-tournament.html|title=Villanova Wipes Out Oklahoma and a Record to Reach the Title Game|last=Tracy|first=Marc|date=2016-04-02|work=The New York Times|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}} In the National Championship game, they defeated No. 1 seed [[2015–16 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] to earn the second NCAA Championship title in school history, the first since [[1985 NCAA Division I baseball tournament|1985]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/04/05/sports/ncaabasketball/unc-villanova-national-championship.html|title=Villanova Wins N.C.A.A.
